descriptionChirho: The inner person as the seat of thought, understanding, volition, emotion, and moral character; the core of human consciousness and intentionality, encompassing what English distinguishes as mind, will, conscience, and feelings. Universally glossed as corazón (Spa), हृदय/दिल/मन (Hin), قلب (Arb), 마음 (Kor), moyo (Swa) across all inflections and prepositional frames.

The physical interior or central core of a non-personal entity, as in 'the heart of the sea' or 'the heart of the heavens'; a spatial/locative extension distinct from the anthropological inner-self sense, evidenced by Swahili katikati ya ('middle of') and Korean 가슴 ('chest/breast') rather than the usual 마음 ('mind').

Adjectival use meaning whole, complete, or sound, describing a heart that is undivided and fully devoted; glossed as íntegro (Spa), पूरे (Hin), سَلِيم (Arb), 온전한 (Kor), kamili (Swa), marking an attributive or predicative quality rather than the noun 'heart' itself.
